title: Unwind Safety Assumptions in Panic-Abort Crates
pattern: Relying on custom `Drop` destructors to perform critical, external state cleanup (like flushing caches, closing network sockets, or releasing hardware lock resources) under panic unwinding, while compiling the crate with `panic = "abort"`.
why_bad: If the crate is compiled with `panic = "abort"`, stack unwinding is completely bypassed on panic. The process terminates immediately without executing any destructors, leaving system files, hardware locks, or database caches in a corrupted, half-written state.
detection: A crate relies on stack unwinding destructors to maintain global or external consistency invariants, but allows configuration of the global `panic = "abort"` profile.
counterexample: Explicitly checking or documenting that a crate requires `panic = "unwind"`, or writing crash-consistent state handlers.
fix: Document or restrict compilation settings to unwind, or use transactional writes that remain crash-consistent even on unexpected aborts.
source: Rust For Rustaceans, Chapter 10 (panic settings / unwinding) [799-801].
